title: The Dreamland building, Doc Johnson and Bill Bottoms
summary: With her husband's help they work out who owned and managed the Dreamland at 35th and State, its earlier dance-school names, and its redecoration.

story.theme_name: Gangsters, bootleggers and rough clubs of Prohibition
story.community_name: Cabarets, honky-tonks and the Storyville nightlife scene

blocks.x: Well, don't record it at all until I would know, because I can't recall so easily.
Well, actually, it doesn't matter too much, because we'll come upon it in a little while.
Bill Byrne had it a long time, though, before he turned it over to somebody else, didn't he? And then...
I'm trying to think...
Well, he may have given up management just for a short time

or subleased it or something. What I was going to say is, you know, to be truthful about it, Dr. Johnson, Dr. Johnson, I think, it was his building. And I'm thinking after Bill Bottoms, I'm not too sure about this, but I'm thinking Dr. Johnson taking it back over after Bill Bottoms. Mm-hmm.
And then Bill Bottoms taking it back again?
No. Mm-hmm. No. Bill never taking it back again.
There are some very early notes about the dancing school being there before it was made into... Yes.
Into a nightclub.
Nightclub. Now, this goes back to maybe the years maybe before you were in Chicago. When did you come into Chicago?
Oh, good. I was here before the dreamland. So, I'm thinking that is really the time that May Alex started...
At the dream.

At the dreamland. She... May Alex was a schoolgirl then, and I'm thinking that LaRue was managing the club, and May Alex, I think, was going... At the bottom. ...was going to key school, and we was having those... Those...
Amateurs?
Amateurs. Amateurs. Oh, yeah. Amateurs there. Oh, and she won Amateurs? And LaRue was managing. I'm not too sure too much about it. It's been a long time.
Well, here's something in 1915. Deluxe Dancing Academy... Well, the Deluxe happened to be across the street later on, but notice, Deluxe Dancing Academy, Garfield Wilson's Orchestra,
Dreamland Hall. That was upstairs. The Deluxe was upstairs.

Yes, but Dreamland Hall, 3520 State. That's right. That would have made it the Dreamland. That was the Dreamland. But they called it Deluxe Dancing Academy. Yeah. So that name Deluxe tossed about a little bit before they named the Deluxe across the street.
I don't recall that.
See, the...
The only Deluxe... The only Deluxe that I recall was across the street, upstairs.
On the east side of the street. On the east side of the street.
Well, here's another note. Eli Dancing School introducing the Foxtrot every Wednesday night at Johnson's Dreamland Hall.
Well, now, that's Dr. Johnson, yeah.
35th and State.

That was Doc Johnson, yeah. Yeah, that was Doc Johnson. See, he owned that building, and he... And I remember that Bill Bottoms was a part of that building under the supervision of Doc Johnson. Mm-hmm. See? So... And I'm thinking... See, it was two brothers of those Johnsons, and the older brother owned the building. And in the later years, the younger brother, the big tall fellow of Dr. Johnson, is as close as I can recall.
Was Bottoms responsible for the redecoration and putting in a raised bandstand and finding glass floor and so forth? Do you think that...
I'm thinking that he was. I mean, that was...
At least the building...

Putting in the glass inside and that. I'm thinking that Bill was responsible for that. And coming from the doctor, which was his property, I'm thinking that he helped the program. They worked together on that. Yeah.
Well, it must have been a moneymaker because they invested several times
in redecorating. Oh, it was a great... It was a great thing there. Oh, yeah. It was a great thing there. I mean, I mean, not for one year, but for many years.
Several years.
Yeah. So it was a moneymaker and a beautiful building.
Yeah, it was.
Very beautiful building.
